saints.name: St. Christopher Magallanes and Companions
saints.title: Priests and Martyrs
saints.shortBlurb: A Mexican parish priest and his fellow martyrs, killed in the persecution of the Church during the Cristero years…
biography: Cristóbal Magallanes Jara was born to farming parents at San Rafael, Totatiche, in Jalisco on 30 July 1869, and worked as a shepherd before entering the seminary of Guadalajara. Ordained in 1899, he was made parish priest of his native Totatiche, where he founded schools and carpentry shops and gave himself to the evangelization of the Huichol people.

When the government closed the seminary of Guadalajara, he opened a clandestine house of studies, the Auxiliary Seminary of Totatiche, in 1915. Though he wrote and preached against armed rebellion, he was accused of fomenting the Cristero rising; arrested on 21 May 1927 while on his way to celebrate Mass, he was shot without trial at Colotlán four days later, with the young priest Agustín Caloca, prefect of his seminary.

He gave his few possessions to his executioners, absolved them, and declared: 'I die innocent, and ask God that my blood may serve to unite my Mexican brethren.' Beatified in 1992, he was canonized by John Paul II on 21 May 2000 with twenty-four companions, priests and laymen martyred in the persecution of the Church in Mexico between 1915 and 1937.
saints.knownFor: Faithful priests martyred in Mexico's persecution of the Church.
